svg.text: How City Air Tracker works
One route from 50 cities to a live dashboard. Plain English on top, the technical details in the gray boxes.
START
The goal: check the air quality in any of 50 U.S. cities, for any day.
SETUP
Pick the cities
One city for every U.S. state, 50 in total. For each one we look up exactly
where it is on the map.
city_table.py · OpenWeather Geocoding API · saves city_table.json
adds ",US" to every query so "AL" is not read as Albania, the country
SETUP
Build a home for the data
A database in the cloud (on AWS) with two tables: one for the cities and
one for the air quality readings.
create_table.py + insert_cities.py · PostgreSQL on AWS RDS
city_table (50 rows) and air_pollution_table (about 290k rows)
COLLECT
Ask for the air quality
For every city we ask OpenWeather for the air quality, one reading for
every hour of the day.
daily_info.py, load_day() · OpenWeather Air Pollution API
50 cities x 24 hours = 1,200 rows a day, a failed request skips that city
COLLECT
Tidy it up and save it
The names are cleaned up, the times are put on one standard clock, and the
readings are saved. Saving the same day twice never creates doubles.
field names mapped (co to carbon_monoxide), Unix time converted to UTC
INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on a unique (city_id, reading_time_utc)
COLLECT
Fill in the past
We load every day from January 1, 2026 up to yesterday, so there is history
to look back on.
backfill.py · Jan 1, 2026 to yesterday
new connection and commit each day, so one dropped connection loses little
COLLECT
Keep it fresh
Every morning at 6am the newest day is added automatically. Nobody has to
press a button.
cron · 0 6 * * * · runs daily_info.py for yesterday
SHOW
Show it on a dashboard
Pick a city and a date and see the air quality as a gauge, charts, and the
best and worst hours of the day.
myapp.py · Dash + Plotly · reads straight from RDS
shows a message if there is no data, or fewer than 24 hours for that day
SHOW
Ask the AI
Type a question like “Is it safe to exercise outside today?” and get a plain
English answer based on that city’s real readings.
bot.py · Gemini API
the prompt is built from the selected city’s readings, so answers stay grounded
SHARE
Put it online
The app lives on the web (on Render), and the database only lets approved
visitors in, so the data stays safe.
Render web service · same live URL
RDS security group allows only approved IPs, keys live in environment variables
FINISH
Anyone can open it and check the air before heading outside:
city-air-tracker.onrender.com
